title: Saffron AI - Postmortem + Preventive Hardenings Sync
summary: Review of the June 30th production outage impacting inference latency for Saffron's chat widget, discussion of interim mitigations (traffic shaping + fallback model), deep-dive into root cause (KV cache eviction pattern + autoscaler mis-config), and agreement on preventive hardenings and monitoring additions. Security questions on audit logs and KMS integration were clarified; next steps and owners assigned.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-22
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 1h 4m
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Darla Nguyen (Redwood CSM), Priya Patel (CTO - Saffron), Evan Lowe (Platform), Marta Ruiz (Security), Jonah Park (SRE), Aisha Khan (Product)

Summary: quick sync to go over the June 30th outage, what changed in infra, immediate mitigations, and plan to prevent recurrence plus follow-ups on security artifacts.

[00:00] Lena (Redwood AE): okay everyone, thanks for joining on short notice, uh we wanted to walk through the postmortem and make sure owners and dates are clear. Marcus is gonna take us through the deep-dive but quick context: saffron saw a cascade increase in tail latency on the chat widget starting ~14:12 UTC on June 30, customer traffic hit fallback for ~38 minutes and there was some user-impact.

[00:22] Priya (Saffron CTO): yes that's right, we had around an 18% error rate for the widget, some sessions timed out. We activated fallback to smaller model and that recovered UX but cost and consistency hit.

[00:37] Marcus (Redwood SE): i'll share my screen after, but quick tl;dr — two things aligned: a subtle eviction pattern in the KV cache under a certain prefix distribution plus autoscale cooldowns on the Dedicated pool not tuned for the burst profile. So we got amplification: cold KV hits causing longer token latency and then fewer instances coming up fast enough, so requests piled up and backend thresholds were exceeded.

[01:05] Jonah (SRE): just to clarify, the autoscaler delayed adding capacity because of the 5m averaging window, right? we had sustained 90% GPU util for like 3 minutes but the scaler considered it transient.

[01:20] Marcus: yeah exactly, the policy used a 5-minute lookback and step increase of 1 per 2 minutes; with this traffic shape that wasn't fast enough. The kv cache eviction we saw was due to a prefix hotset where repeated unseen contexts evicted earlier prefixes because of LRU-ish behavior — we think the workload shifted after a release with longer prompts.

[01:48] Evan (Platform): to add, our release did change system prompts for the chat which increased avg seq length. We missed simulating that change during load tests. That was on us.

[02:05] Marta (Security): quick sec question — were any logs or PII spilled to third-party telemetry during the spike? we got compliance alerts and want to confirm retention and access controls.

[02:20] Darla (Redwood CSM): good question, Marta. From Redwood side we only saw internal traces and metrics; no transcript content left our dedicated pool or was sent to external analytics. We'll share audit logs showing the storage access events, and Lena will follow up with the exact indices.

[02:40] Priya: okay thanks. can you also confirm KMS usage for keys is still enforced in our Private deployment? we had a few concerns from the security review that might be related.

[02:55] Marcus: your deployment is configured with customer-managed KMS and HSM-backed keys; our onboarding notes show key rotation at 90 days and all inference artifacts are encrypted at rest. We'll attach the KMS proof artifacts, but Darla will push the short checklist.

[03:15] Lena: Marcus, can you go through the timeline and the logs you pulled?

[03:22] Marcus: sure. so timeline — 14:10 traffic jump, 14:12 tail lat grows, 14:14 first autoscale trigger but cooldown prevented immediate upscale, 14:16 kv eviction surge starts, 14:20 queueing grows and some 503s seen by the edge, 14:48 fallback to smaller model completed and steady state by 14:58. I have snippets of kernel traces showing stalls around the attention kernel at the high sequence lengths, and batch sizes collapsed which amplified per-token cost.

[04:05] Evan: are these kernel stalls visible in our monitoring? we didn't see obvious GPU errors.

[04:12] Marcus: they're subtle — not driver errors, more like poor kernel selection for the shape we ran. The runtime picked a path optimized for shorter sequences, then under the long prompt it fell back to a generic kernel that cost more, and the KV cache churn increased memory pressure on the host, which produced scheduling jitter.

[04:40] Aisha (Product): sorry, a dumb question — the KV cache is per-request or shared? because if its shared then eviction could hurt unrelated sessions, correct?

[04:51] Marcus: not dumb — the KV cache is sharded per model variant but shared across requests to maximize reuse; eviction policies are LRU-adjacent and can inadvertently evict hot prefixes when the distribution skews suddenly.

[05:10] Priya: so is the short-term fix to increase cache size? or is it to change eviction? what's the recommended immediate mitigation?

[05:20] Marcus: immediate mitigations we recommend: 1) traffic shaping / staged canary to limit burst; 2) increase KV cache pre-warm for the new system prompts OR pin a small hotset; 3) reduce autoscaler lookback window and allow a faster step increase for Saffron's workload; 4) enable an aggressive fallback to a quantized variant just for spikes. We actually pushed a temporary config for you during the outage which is why fallback worked.

[05:56] Priya: that worked, but it increased token cost by ~22% for the week — need to get this under control.

[06:05] Lena: absolutely. part of today's plan is to get benchmarking numbers for the tuned dedicated pool so we can propose an ops config that meets your SLOs and cost targets. Marcus, can you explain the tuned autoscale recommendation?

[06:17] Marcus: recommended autoscale: use a 60s lookback with 30s evaluation buckets for short-burst workloads, allow ramp steps of 2 instances per minute up to a cap, and add a pro-active pre-warm hook based on deploy events. Also, set a reserve percentage to keep one spare instance up during peak windows.

[06:45] Jonah: two quick items — we want an observable SLI for kv eviction rate and an alert when eviction spikes > X per minute. Can we get that?

[06:52] Marcus: yes, we can add eviction_rate metric and an alert rule; we'll also add a dashboard tile for batch size distribution, kernel selection heatmap and GPU stall counts.

[07:10] Marta: for compliance, we need immutable audit logs for the fallback switch and the time-limited access changes during remediation. Can Redwood provide an exportable audit trail?

[07:20] Darla: yes, Redwood's private control plane keeps immutable audit entries for admin actions, model rollouts, and fallback triggers. We'll produce a filtered export for the incident timeframe.

[07:36] Evan: about testing — we'll run the dedicated pool benchmark that mirrors the new prompts. what config should we use for the test to be meaningful?

[07:44] Marcus: run with sequence length distribution matching production: mean 64 tokens, 99th percentile 220 tokens, growth spikes to 400 tokens in some sessions. Use concurrent sessions ~120 and ramp ramp profile of 5 minutes to simulate release traffic. Use the same model variant you deploy. We'll share the benchmark script.

[08:10] Priya: what about long-term code changes — do we need to change our prompts to avoid the churn? product doesn't want to degrade UX but we can consider shorter contexts, or chunking.

[08:22] Aisha: yeah product's open to re-evaluating the system prompt, maybe move some deterministic instructions client-side so the model sees fewer tokens. We'll run feasibility.

[08:36] Marcus: great. long-term hardenings we propose: adaptive cache sizing, more robust kernel selection heuristics in runtime, autoscaler policy improvements, and a pre-deploy simulation that triggers pre-warm hooks if avg seq length changes >20%.

[09:05] Priya: do you have any timeline for runtime kernel heuristics? is that a drop-in fix or an engineering cycle?

[09:12] Marcus: it's non-trivial; some heuristics can be toggled in config in weeks, deeper kernel optimization is months. We'll prioritize config toggles and a canary release to test improvements.

[09:30] Marta: small items on security — can we formalize acceptance criteria for the fallback path: encryption in transit, audit visibility, RBAC restrictions? we need that for our compliance sign-off.

[09:45] Darla: yes we'll draft an acceptance checklist covering TLS endpoints, KMS key IDs used, audit log entries for fallback, and RBAC scope for on-call users.

[09:58] Lena: alright let's recap owners and dates — Marcus: kernel traces and eviction logs by 7/24; Darla: audit export + KMS checklist by 7/23; Evan: dedicated pool benchmark results by 7/29; Priya: confirm canary fraction by 7/25; Lena: runbook + staged rollback proposal by 7/24. Any additions?

[10:20] Priya: sounds good. also can we set a quick 30-min follow-up the week after the benchmark to go over numbers?

[10:28] Lena: yes, let's pencil 7/31 16:00 UTC for a results review. Darla will send invites.

[10:40] Jonah: one more ask — can we get a sample of the fallback latency profile so we can plan UX messaging?

[10:48] Marcus: will include percentile latency for the quantized variant in the benchmark output.

[10:55] Lena: thanks everyone, we'll share artifacts to the incident channel and follow up on the action items.

[11:00] Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: transcription contains some name mismatches in places and occasional dropped words; speakers are labeled by role where available.
